_doc: Release notes for the in-app "What's new" sheet (public/whats-new.js). Newest first, keyed by package.json version. `highlights` are the features (the main stage); each may carry a `visual` (timeline | glyph) and a `try` action (settings:<section id> | tab:<type> | split | palette | copy:<text>). `fixes` is a list of one-line strings (bug fixes and small improvements, inline `code` allowed) shown on a secondary page behind a footer button. A fixes-only release omits `highlights` (and may omit `title`/`summary`); upgrading to only fixes-only releases shows a toast instead of opening the sheet.

fixes: Maximizing a pane that sits inside a split (e.g. the bottom-right one) now fills the whole window instead of just its column.

releases.title: See what got fixed
releases.summary: Release notes now list bug fixes too, on their own page, so you can check whether the thing that bugged you is sorted.

highlights.title: Fixes & improvements page
highlights.body: Features stay front and centre here. Bug fixes and small improvements sit one click away behind the button at the bottom of this sheet. Updates that only bring fixes no longer open the sheet; a toast tells you instead.

fixes: Releases that only contain fixes show a short toast after updating instead of opening this sheet.

Terminal apps such as Claude Code, vim or htop sometimes drew into a corner of the pane until you nudged a divider. Another open Meowtrix window or device could shrink the active session's terminals; now only the active session sizes them, and a resize lost while reconnecting is re-sent.
Terminal tabs failed to open (`Terminal is not defined`) when the server was older than the page, e.g. after pulling an update without restarting. The bundled terminal now falls back to the CDN copy.
Desktop builds of 1.33.0 reported the wrong version, so the updater kept offering the update you already had.
Upgrading from a version before this sheet existed now shows the latest release notes.

releases.title: Faster under heavy output
releases.summary: Busy terminals, divider drags and background scans now cost a fraction of what they did. Each change can be switched off in Settings → Performance.

highlights.title: Batched terminal output
highlights.body: When a build log or an agent floods the terminal, output is grouped into one message every 10 ms instead of one per chunk. Typing and prompts aren't batched, so echo stays instant.

highlights.title: Smooth pane resizing
highlights.body: Dragging a divider used to tell every shell about its new size on every frame, so vim, htop and agent TUIs redrew constantly. Now they redraw once you pause.

visual.caption: Resize signals sent to the shell during one drag

highlights.title: Quieter port detection
highlights.body: The scan for new dev-server ports runs every 10 seconds instead of every 2, and stops entirely while no Meowtrix page is visible. The interval is yours to choose.

highlights.title: Snappier startup
highlights.body: The terminal libraries now load from your own server instead of a CDN, so pages open faster over tunnels and work offline. The code editor's loader waits until you open an editor.

releases.title: Native browser tabs
releases.summary: In the desktop app, browser tabs are real native webviews instead of a proxied frame, so sign-ins and heavy sites just work.

highlights.title: Browser tabs use a native webview
highlights.body: Sites that refuse to be embedded, use strict cookies, or need full WebSocket support now render as they would in a normal browser. Outside the desktop app the proxy is still used.

visual.caption: Desktop app only · Settings → Browser to switch back

releases.title: Host browser and the agent bridge
releases.summary: Drive a real Chromium on the host from any device, and let coding agents open pages and files beside you.

highlights.title: Host browser tabs
highlights.body: A real Chromium runs on the host and streams to your tab, with its own persistent profile. Use it for sites the proxy can't handle, like Google sign-in.

visual.caption: Streams from the host · works from your phone

highlights.title: mtx agent bridge
highlights.body: Agents running in a terminal can call `mtx open <url>`, `mtx edit <file>` or `mtx notify`, or use them as MCP tools, and the result opens in a pane next to the agent.

visual.caption: Register the MCP server once per agent

releases.title: CoDesign review loop
releases.summary: Review an agent's living spec visually, pin comments to elements, and sign off — all without leaving Meowtrix.

highlights.title: CoDesign tabs
highlights.body: An agent writes `.codesign/spec.html` and runs `mtx review`. You pin comments on the rendered page and press Send feedback; the agent picks them up and revises.
